title: Rhode Island beach house with water views on both sides — can you guess the price?
author: Emily Turner
bullets: The Westerly, Rhode Island beach house features a contemporary cottage style and was built in 1987.
The 2,724-square-foot property includes 3 bedrooms, 3 full baths, and offers water views on both sides.
Annual taxes for the house amount to $11,125 as of 2025, with the listing price options ranging from $1.78 to $1.98 million.

title: 5 best new restaurant openings and dining updates in Boston (August 13, 2026)
author: Nathan Tavares
bullets: First Crush, a natural wine bar by Gabrielle Malina, opens mid-September at 259 Washington St., Somerville.
Chef Jeff Almendras turns his Filipino-inspired sandwich popup into a restaurant at 300 Summer St., Seaport, this fall.
The Temp Agency, an office-themed bar by Tiffani Faison, opens at High Street Place, Downtown Boston, this August.

title: 3 concerning trends from Red Sox’ 5-game losing skid
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: The Red Sox have lost five consecutive games after a strong mid-season performance, struggling against non-playoff teams.
Boston's offense is faltering, averaging 2.8 runs per game in the last five, with key players like Willson Contreras underperforming.
The bullpen, including Tyron Guerrero and Aroldis Chapman, is facing setbacks, with concerns over Garrett Whitlock's elbow inflammation.

title: An Easton church has been converted to a $1.3m home
author: Megan Johnson
bullets: The former Swedish Evangelical Lutheran Church at 16 Williams St., Easton, is now a home listed for $1.3 million.
The 5,730-square-foot residence features four bedrooms, three-and-a-half bathrooms, and retains original church design elements.
Converted in 2008, the property includes a gourmet kitchen, great room with stained glass, and primary suite with spa bathroom.

title: Blue Jays erupt for 5 runs in the eighth to beat Red Sox 6-4, extend Boston’s skid to 5
author: The Associated Press
bullets: The Toronto Blue Jays scored five runs in the eighth inning to defeat the Boston Red Sox 6-4.
Kazuma Okamoto's RBI single and Myles Straw's two-run double highlighted Toronto's eighth-inning rally.
Boston's Willson Contreras hit his 24th home run, but the Red Sox have now lost five straight games.

title: Allston-Brighton residents divided over future of Jackson Mann Community Center, survey shows
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Survey shows Allston-Brighton residents are divided on Jackson Mann Community Center's redevelopment options, lacking clear consensus.
190 residents prefer housing, 171 a school, and 124 both in the proposed redevelopment options for the center.
Mayor Michelle Wu to decide the center's future by year-end, with another survey open until September 10 for community feedback.

title: Tour the Patriots’ new 160,000-square-foot training facility
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: The New England Patriots unveiled their 160,000-square-foot New Balance Athletics Center next to Gillette Stadium.
Facilities include a 15,000-square-foot weight room, a virtual reality room, and a 92-locker room for players.
The center features a dining area, hydrotherapy room, player’s lounge, and space for future modifications.

title: Man killed in stabbing inside South Station during rush hour, officials say
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: A man was fatally stabbed at Boston's South Station during rush hour on Wednesday evening.
The altercation occurred on an escalator; the victim died after being taken to a local hospital.
Police are searching for a male suspect and reviewing video footage, urging witnesses to come forward.

title: Body found at TD Garden, police say
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: Boston police found a deceased person near TD Garden around 5:15 p.m. Wednesday.
The body was reportedly in a parking garage adjacent to TD Garden, according to preliminary information.
The incident is under investigation, with Boston police handling inquiries about the case.

title: Athol man charged with child pornography possession
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: Kristopher Ambrozewicz, 35, from Athol, was charged with possession of child sexual abuse materials, according to federal prosecutors.
Authorities seized electronics, including laptops, at Ambrozewicz's home after discovering child sexual abuse videos on his phone.
Ambrozewicz, also working for a behavioral health center, faces up to 20 years in prison if convicted.
